result_title.text: UNICEF supported closing the polio outbreak response in Papua and led key assessments including the expanded programme on immunization review and demand generation activities. UNICEF continues supporting malaria elimination efforts and is transitioning out of direct support in four provinces (Aceh, South Sulawesi, West Sulawesi, North Maluku) due to very successful achievements. UNICEF will concentrate its support in the highest burden provinces: Papua, Papua Barat, NTT, Maluku for the next five years. Extensive support has also been provided for ensuring continuity of malaria, HIV and immunization services during COVID-19 as well as preparation for the COVID-19 vaccine rollout.

result_title.text: National and sub-national governments remain strongly committed with enhanced capacity to improve access to quality, inclusive education for out-of-school children (OOSC) and children with disabilities (CWD). Good practices from the OOSC and inclusive education programmes contributed to the development of provincial action plans for the programmes replication in other areas. With UNICEF's direct support, around 26,770 OOSC (44% girls, 95% adolescents) have enrolled back in school through formal or non-formal education. In addition, around 402,000 children with and without disabilities (48.4% girls, 3.5% with disabilities) have learned social inclusion values (e.g. respect, teamwork, tolerance) through physical education and sports.

result_title.text: The Government and UNRCO acknowledge UNICEF’s technical contributions to developing the 9th NSEDP results framework at the 13th High-level round table meeting in November 2021. Laos co-hosted an innovative solution for child poverty at a side event during the 76th UNGA. With support from UNICEF and the EU, the Government launched an interactive web-based platform for monitoring nutrition results and investments in the country. In addition, the third round of the Lao Social Indicator Survey, through a high-level partnership engagement, mobilized 72 % of resources for the survey.  Country capacity for child poverty analysis was established for tracking child-related deprivations.

result_title.text: The unprecedented crisis caused by COVID-19 has marked the year 2021, with the country’s immunization programme having had to face disruptions, especially during the lockdown period. Recognizing the country's challenging operating environment, UNICEF significantly increased efforts ensuring the country's immunization programme is maintained. A total of 50 poor-performing districts received UNICEF funding to ensure a continuity of essential health services, particularly immunization. Since the pandemic's longer-term trajectory remains uncertain, as part of UNICEF’s commitment to immunization and health system strengthening, efforts focused on further enhancing the Cold Chain System Strengthening and scale up of the COVID-19 vaccine.

result_title.text: Overall, there has been good progress in the implementation of the WASH program. In 2020, UNICEF’s direct WASH interventions in communities and institutions have given 80,417 persons access to improved water, sanitation and hygiene services in all the 13 municipalities in Timor-Leste improving the standard of life and resilience against COVID19 and natural disasters while 44 communities (sub villages) became open defecation free. The WASH program has been boosted by the COVID-19 response interventions, especially the promotion of handwashing with soap and clean water. However, the availability of water remains a key challenge.

result_title.text: UNICEF and its partners continued to expandg climate-resilient WASH services across Chipinge, Mangwe, Beitbridge and Harare districts. During the first half of 2026, eight  (8) solar-powered piped water systems and rehabilitated 15 boreholes significantly , improving access to safe and reliable water for vulnerable communities. Thirty Water Point User Committees were trained on Drinking Water Safety and Security Planning, while water quality monitoring was undertaken across the four districts. Community-led sanitation interventions supported 30 communities working towards Open Defecation Free status, 15 school sanitation blocks were completed, and eight (8) health facilities were upgraded using the WASHFIT approach. These interventions strengthened sustainability, resilience and inclusiveness of WASH service delivery across communities, schools and health facilities

result_title.text: In 2026, UNICEF advanced child-centered climate policy, planning and advocacy in Zimbabwe, contributing to improved resilience of children, young people, and their families to climate change. UNICEF supported the integration of child sensitivity into two (2) national and international climate and environment policy processes, exceeding the annual target of 1. These included the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0 Elaboration, to be submitted to UNFCCC in September 2026, the National Climate Change Management Bill, reinforcing a national commitment to putting children at the centre of climate action. Children and young people actively shaped these processes, including contributions by 60 children to NDC 3.0 elaboration stakeholder consultations. Evidence generation resulted in one child-sensitive Children Climate Risk Index, while 3000 young climate advocates were engaged through local, subnational, national and international platforms. Sub-national initiatives further amplified children's voices through environment clubs, experiential learning and structured coordination under the KOICA supported project Climate Action for the Last Mile (CALM).

result_title.text: In 2026, UNICEF continued to strengthen Zimbabwe's child protection policy and institutional environment. Four laws and policies were influenced to strengthen child protection safeguards, representing significant progress toward the annual target. The ongoing supported laws include the review of the Social Workers Act, the Birth and Deaths Registration Act, finalization of the DNA Evidence Bill and the Child Justice Bill. UNICEF is also supporting the establishment of a Sexual Offenders Register, with consultations having already taken place.  UNICEF's advocacy resulted in the approval of two major child protection documents, the National Action for Children IV and the Child Online Protection Policy, both running from 2026-2030. Protection Conference where these landmark documents were launched, with the Conference calling for sustainable child protection financing, among other key outcomes. UNICEF continued its leadership in supporting CRVS with this year's highlight in participating in the Africa Continental CRVS conference in Vic Falls which defined new CRVS priorities for AU member States.

result_title.text: In 2026, UNICEF continued to ensure that children and adolescents, including the most vulnerable, have access to equitable, quality, and inclusive child protection and GBV prevention and response services. Strong progress was recorded under Output 6.2 during the first half of 2026. A total of 36,196 (17,322M;18,864F) children who experienced violence were reached through health, social work and justice services, representing approximately 90 per cent of the annual target. Birth registration services reached 23,952 (11,847M; 12,105F) children, significantly exceeding annual targets at mid-year. Community-based mental health and psychosocial support services reached 49,835 (19,173M; 30,662F) children, adolescents, parents and caregivers, while social mobilization and awareness interventions engaged the same number of mothers, fathers, community members, boys and girls. In addition, 5,465 adolescent girls benefited from child marriage prevention and response interventions. These results demonstrate continued progress in strengthening service access, prevention efforts and community-based child protection systems.

UNICEF also supported the implementation of the Zimbabwe Early Learning Assessment  2025, which assessed foundational literacy and numeracy competencies of learners at the end of Grade 2, generating critical evidence to inform improvements in teaching and learning. To inform the Education Sector Strategic Plan (2026 2030) development. the Education Sector Analysis  is now completed

A combination of the cash transfer mechanism put in place by UNICEF, routine monitoring and community engagement ensured regular monthly electronic cash transfer to beneficiaries across the 3 focused districts despite the COVID-19 lockdown measures.

result_title.text: Rehabilitation of 991 water sources, including borehole repairs and reprogramming to piped water schemes, by UNICEF resulted in basic water supply services for 483,626 people (52.9% females; including 7,371 people with disabilities). Construction of 1,452 self-sponsored household latrines and 765 subsidized latrines for vulnerable households contributed to additional 11,564 rural people (52.6% females) using basic sanitation services and nine villages (45% of target) becoming open defecation free. Institutional WASH services in 457 schools also benefitted 250,988 students (52% female) and contributed to an increased in the proportion of schools with basic water services from 64% (2017) to 67% in 2021.

result_title.text: Despite the COVID-19 pandemic, there was increase in coverage in most maternal and newborn indicators in 2021. Through UNICEF’s inputs, 93% of Primary Health Care facilities are providing the 5 signal functions of Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care and 92% of district hospitals are providing Comprehensive Obstetric and Newborn Care. Significant achievements included completion of the draft WASH Climate Strategy pending validation, development of operational and maintenance guidance for WASH in health facilities, completion of a costed WASH-in-HCF roadmap.  Additionally UNICEF continued support to district and national coordination mechanisms through joint monitoring visits, quarterly reviews and district coordination meetings. These efforts strengthened institutional capacity to plan, monitor and sustain climate-resilient WASH services while improving integration of climate adaptation considerations across sector planning and implementation.

result_title.text: Zimbabwe has maintained the global targets towards ending AIDS by 2030. However, children, adolescents and young women continue to face age and gender-related inequities. From January to June 2026, UNICEF trained 59 healthcare workers in PMTCT, paediatric HIV,  and integrated service delivery, strengthening case identification, referral, and linkage to care. This contributed to, 36,393 children and adolescents living with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy, while 24,230 pregnant and breastfeeding women accessed medicines to prevent vertical transmission. Service integration also improved ANC enrolment, immunization and early infant HIV diagnosis and treatment.

result_title.text: The co-leadership of UNICEF and the Government of the national social protection coordination architecture resulted in new evidence generation on targeting, development of the social protection Management Information System and introduction of disability inclusiveness to the national programme to improve institutional capacity. UNICEF’s advocacy and technical assistance to the Ministry of Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare resulted in the release of 97% (US$10.9 million) of the harmonized social cash transfers (HSCT) payments against a target of 70%. This allocation benefitted 1.5 million children including 129,557 households (above the target of 29,000) directly supported by UNICEF.

result_title.text: In 2021, UNICEF’s leadership of the Child Protection Working Group, the training of 280 community case workers and implementation of the community-based Gender-Based Violence in Emergency (GBViE) risk mitigation strategy resulted in 132,243 children (55% girls) accessing critical child protection in emergency (CPiE) services to respond to multi hazards and vulnerabilities associated with drought, residual effects of cyclone Idai and COVID-19. The CPiE services provided included family tracing, reunification, and appropriate follow up care for UASC; emergency shelter, counselling mental health and psychosocial support, and legal assistance for victims of GBV; and birth registration outreach services in COVID-19 hotspots.

result_title.text: Over 1.7 million learners benefited from UNICEF-supported radio and TV lessons to mitigate the COVID-19 impact. Since its launch in March, the UNICEF-supported Learning Passport – a collaboration with the Government and Microsoft - has reached 79,560 users, and more than 3,700 local content lessons and materials have been developed and uploaded on the Learning Passport. The roll-out of the offline version of the Learning Passport in 50 schools has started and will benefit 56,926 learners (29,619 girls). More than 3,700 schools have improved WASH facilities for 1,346,390 children (672,072 girls), assisting them to better address and mitigate COVID-19
